This task doesn't require deep Minecraft crafting knowledge — it's primarily a navigation and visual recognition task. It's well-suited for a single-task benchmark because success is easily measurable (the agent gets close enough to the iron door and looks at it). The iron door is visually distinctive, making it a good candidate for testing an agent's ability to explore and identify objects in a Minecraft environment.

milestones.description: Uses position_near_with_facing because this is a find/locate task. The player must navigate close to the iron door (within 5 blocks) and face toward it. The iron door is at relative position (8, 1, 6) on the south face of the stone brick building. This rule checks both proximity and facing direction, correctly modeling 'the player has found and is looking at the iron door'.

scene_description: A small stone brick outpost with an iron door is placed about 8-10 blocks from spawn in the +X/+Z direction. The scene includes several minor decorative structures (oak planks shed, cobblestone wall, oak fences, a lantern, and a Guide armor stand) to add visual complexity. The player must explore the area and locate the iron door on the south-facing wall of the stone brick building.
task_text: Find the iron door in the area. Explore the surroundings and navigate to the iron door.
design_notes: The iron door is at relative position (~8, ~1-2, ~6), facing south, embedded in a 5x5 stone brick building. The player spawns at the origin facing the general direction of the building. The door is the only iron door in the scene, making it unambiguous. A stone button is placed next to the door for realism. Other structures (oak shed, cobblestone wall, fences) add visual complexity. The building is ~10 blocks from spawn — close enough to find within 20 steps but requires deliberate exploration.
